title: How much cheaper must a store's electricity be than a heat pump's for a sand heat store to deliver heat for less?
summary: Costs the sand store of energy-thermal with every capital cost, lifetime, O&M and efficiency read from PyPSA technology-data (Danish Energy Agency; Viswanathan et al. 2022, PNNL-33283) at pinned revisions, sizing it with the transient model and comparing levelised cost of heat against an air-source heat pump. A sand store charged at EUR 0.05/kWh beats a heat pump when the pump's electricity costs about 2 times as much if the store cycles daily, 5 times weekly, 16 times monthly and 120 times seasonally (house, 10 MWh a year; 222 m3 and EUR 1.53 of capital per kWh for the seasonal store); at district size (5 GWh a year) 2.2, 2.8, 5.3 and 38 times. At 3 times the store can stand 2 days (house) or 7 (district); at 10 times, 14 or 60. A district hot-water tank beats sand for monthly and seasonal storage. Not from a source: electricity prices (swept), 2,000 full-load hours, 0.5 m insulation, cycle counts. Limitations: the sand-store cost is a utility-scale figure, no heat exchanger is costed (favours the store), flat prices, constant COP, instant discharge.
lede: how much cheaper must electricity be for a sand heat store to beat a heat pump? Sourced costs (PyPSA technology-data) on the `energy-thermal` model: a daily-cycled store needs the pump's electricity about 2 times dearer, weekly 5, monthly 16, seasonal 120 (house); the heat lost in standby, not the sand, rules out seasonal storage.
